paper.title: Adaptive Exploration in Linear Contextual Bandit

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic K-armed contextual linear bandit with M discrete contexts
unmapped: Finite set of M contexts drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution p with p(m)>0 for all m
Each context m has a known finite action set A^m in R^d with |A^m|=K that spans R^d
settings.definition_quote: We consider the stochastic $K$-armed contextual linear bandit with a horizon of $n$ rounds and $M$ possible contexts. ... For each context $m \in [M]$ there is a known feature/action set $\cA^m\subset \mathbb R^d$ with $|\cA^m| = K$. ... the environment samples a sequence of independent contexts $(c_t)_{t=1}^n$ from an unknown distribution $p$ over $[M]$ ... The reward is $Y_t = \langle X_t,\theta \rangle + \eta_t$, where $(\eta_t)$ is a sequence of independent standard Gaussian random variables ... we assume each $\cA^{m}$ spans $\mathbb R^d$ and $\|x\|_2\leq1$.

algorithms.name: LinUCB (optimistic policy with beta_t = O(d log t))

symbols.C_lin: C(theta, A^1,...,A^M): value of inf sum_{m,x} alpha_{x,m} Delta_x^m subject to x^T (sum alpha_{x,m} x x^T)^{-1} x <= (Delta_x^m)^2/2 for all suboptimal x

extra_assumptions: optimal arm x_m^* unique for each context

source.label: thm:lower_bound
source.quote: Under the same conditions as \cref{lemma:confidence_width}, \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_{\theta}^{\pi}(n)}{\log(n)}\geq \cC(\theta,\cA^1,\ldots, \cA^M), where $\cC$ is defined as the optimal value of the following optimisation problem: \inf_{\alpha_{x,m}\in[0, \infty]}\sum_{m}\sum_{x}\alpha_{x,m}\Delta_x^m subject to ... x^{\top}(\sum\alpha_{x,m}xx^{\top})^{-1}x \leq \frac{(\Delta_x^m)^2}{2}.

results.notes: Expression means liminf R(n)/log(n) >= C_lin. Constant does not depend on context distribution p. Proof says it follows Corollary 2 of Lattimore & Szepesvari (2017).

symbols.C_lin: C(theta, A^1,...,A^M): optimal value of the lower-bound allocation problem of Theorem 1

extra_assumptions: T_x^m(Delta) uniquely defined and continuous at Delta (uniqueness implies continuity)

source.label: thm:upper_bound
source.quote: Suppose that $T_x^m(\Delta)$ is uniquely defined and $T_x^m(\cdot)$ is continuous at $\Delta$ for all contexts $m$ and actions $x \in \cA^m$. Then the policy $\pi_{\text{oam}}$ proposed in Algorithm \ref{alg:main} with $\epsilon_t = 1/\log(\log(t))$ satisfies \limsup_{n\to \infty}\frac{R_{\theta}^{\pi_{\text{oam}}}(n)}{\log (n)}\leq \cC(\theta, \cA^1,\ldots, \cA^M).

results.notes: Expression means limsup R(n)/log(n) <= C_lin. Algorithm uses f_n which depends on n, so horizon treated as known. Compute: solves a convex program (CVXPY) per round, so polynomial is implied.

bound.regime: optimal arms {x_1^*,...,x_M^*} span R^d; n -> infinity

extra_assumptions: the set of optimal arms {x_1^*, ..., x_M^*} spans R^d
beta_t = O(d log t) suitably chosen

source.label: thm:ucb
source.quote: Consider the policy $\pi$ that plays optimistically by $X_t = \argmax_{x \in \cA^{c_t}} \ip{\hat \theta_{t-1}, x} + \|x\|_{G_t^{-1}} \beta_t^{1/2}$. Suppose that $\theta$ is such that $\{x_1^*, \ldots, x_M^*\}$ spans $\mathbb R^d$. Then, for suitable $(\beta_t)_{t=1}^n$ with $\beta_t = O(d \log(t))$, it holds that $\limsup_{n\to\infty} R_\theta^\pi(n) < \infty$.

results.notes: Bounded regret (limsup finite) recorded as O(1); constant is instance-dependent and unspecified.

cited_results.setting_description: Classical K-armed Gaussian bandit (unit variance), consistent policies; special case M=1, A^1 = standard basis
